walkthroughs.body_html:
Grey Matter — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Grey Matter brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Grey Matter.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of the refractory period after an action potential?
options: It ensures action potentials travel in one direction only and limits the maximum firing frequency.
The refractory period blocks all signals from reaching the neurone.
The refractory period exists because the cell runs out of energy and needs a rest.
Vaccines insert new genes into your DNA permanently.

mcqs.q: What is actually transferred to the body when you get a vaccine?
options: Vaccines insert new genes into your DNA permanently.
Vaccines inject ready-made antibodies directly into the bloodstream.
Antigens (often from weakened, dead, or fragmented pathogens) that train the immune system to make memory cells.
The refractory period blocks all signals from reaching the neurone.

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive conditions more common in males?
options: Vaccines insert new genes into your DNA permanently.
X-linked recessive conditions affect more males because the Y chromosome makes the disease worse.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed — there's no second X to mask it.
X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ester bond”?
options: Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrolysis”?
options: Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Condensation reaction”?
options: Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Polymer”?
options: Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Monomer”?
options: Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glycosidic bond”?
options: Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
